16! =============================================
17! FILE: allio.f90 - TurboRVB Input/Output and Control Module
18! =============================================
19!
20! PURPOSE:
21! This module serves as the central hub for all input/output operations,
22! parameter management, and control variables in TurboRVB quantum Monte Carlo
23! calculations. It defines the complete interface between user input and
24! the computational engine.
25!
26! FILE STRUCTURE:
27! ===============
28!
29! 1. MODULE DECLARATION AND IMPORTS (Lines 15-30)
30! - Module declaration and use statements for dependencies
31! - External module imports (constants, cell, Ewald, types, etc.)
32!
33! 2. VARIABLE DECLARATIONS (Lines 31-1446)
34! - Basic control and configuration variables
35! - System parameters (dimensions, electron counts, etc.)
36! - Optimization and convergence parameters
37! - Physical constants and thresholds
38! - Array declarations for matrices and vectors
39! - Workspace and memory management variables
40! - MPI and parallel computing variables
41! - File I/O and scratch management variables
42!
43! 3. NAMELIST DEFINITIONS (Lines 1447-1940)
44! - /simulation/ : Main simulation control parameters
45! - /pseudo/ : Pseudopotential settings
46! - /readio/ : I/O and file handling options
47! - /vmc/ : Variational Monte Carlo parameters
48! - /dmclrdmc/ : Diffusion Monte Carlo and LR-DMC settings
49! - /optimization/ : Wave function optimization parameters
50! - /parameters/ : Parameter control flags
51! - /fitpar/ : Parameter fitting settings
52! - /dynamic/ : Molecular dynamics parameters
53! - /unused/ : Legacy/unused parameters
54! - /molecul/ : Molecular system settings
55! - /link/ : Link atom parameters
56!
57! 4. SUBROUTINES AND FUNCTIONS (Lines 1959-2561)
58! - scontract_genj() : Matrix contraction for Jastrow factors
59! - scontract_mat_jas() : Jastrow matrix contraction operations
60! - scontract_mat_det() : Determinant matrix contraction operations
61! - update_kgrid() : K-point grid update for periodic systems
62! - norm_metric() : Vector norm calculation using metric tensor
63!
64! 5. STANDALONE SUBROUTINES (Lines 2587-2614)
65! - prep_map() : Lattice vector mapping for periodic systems
66!
67! KEY FEATURES:
68! =============
69! - Comprehensive parameter management for all TurboRVB calculations
70! - Support for both open and periodic boundary conditions
71! - Advanced optimization algorithms (SR, LM, ADAM)
72! - Multi-level parallel computing support (MPI + OpenMP)
73! - Flexible I/O system with scratch file management
74! - Extensive debugging and monitoring capabilities
75!
76! USAGE:
77! ======
78! This module is automatically included in all TurboRVB executables.
79! Users interact with it through namelist input files that define
80! calculation parameters. The module handles parameter validation,
81! default value assignment, and communication between different
82! parts of the code.
83!
84! DEPENDENCIES:
85! =============
86! - constants: Physical constants and mathematical parameters
87! - cell: Unit cell and periodic boundary condition handling
88! - Ewald: Ewald summation for long-range interactions
89! - types: Custom data type definitions
90! - kpoints_mod: K-point sampling and Brillouin zone integration
91! - extpot: External potential and QM/MM interface
92! - van_der_waals: Van der Waals interaction handling
93! - link_atoms: Link atom functionality for QM/MM
94! - sub_comm: Sub-communicator management for parallel computing
95! - mpiio: MPI I/O operations
96! - dielectric: Dielectric continuum models
97!
98! =============================================
99

2027 ! This module contains subroutines for handling I/O operations and data structures
2028 ! The original large allio module has been split into smaller files for faster compilation:
2029 ! - fort10_io.f90: Handles reading/writing of fort.10 files
2030 ! - fort11_io.f90: Handles reading/writing of fort.11 files
2031 ! - read_datas.f90: Reads datas* control files
2032 ! - read_pseudo.f90: Reads pseudopotential files
2033 ! - memOP.f90: Default memory allocation/deallocation operations
2034 ! - writeoutput.f90: Output writing operations
2035
2036 ! Contracts generalized Jastrow matrices
2037 ! Parameters:
2038 ! - nelorbh: Number of orbitals per spin channel
2039 ! - nelorb_c: Number of contracted orbitals
2040 ! - detmat: Output determinant matrix (2*nelorbh x 2*nelorbh)
2041 ! - detmat_c: Input contracted determinant matrix (2*nelorb_c x 2*nelorb_c)
2042 ! - mu_c: Contraction coefficients (nelorbh x nelorb_c)
2043 ! - psip: Temporary workspace (nelorbh x nelorb_c)
2044 subroutine scontract_genj(nelorbh, nelorb_c &
2045 &, detmat, detmat_c, mu_c, psip)
2046 implicit none
2047 integer nelorbh, nelorb, nelorb_c, i
2048 real*8 detmat(2*nelorbh, 2*nelorbh), detmat_c(2*nelorb_c, 2*nelorb_c)&
2049 &, mu_c(nelorbh, *), psip(nelorbh, *)
2050!#ifdef __CASO
2051! nprocu=nprocopt
2052!#else
2053! nprocu=1
2054!#endif
2055 detmat = 0.d0
2056 ! Contract up-up block: detmat(1:nelorbh, 1:nelorbh) = mu_c * detmat_c(1:nelorb_c, 1:nelorb_c) * mu_c^T
2057 call dgemm_my('N', 'N', nelorbh, nelorb_c, nelorb_c, 1.d0, mu_c, nelorbh &
2058 &, detmat_c, 2*nelorb_c, 0.d0, psip, nelorbh, nprocu, rankopt, commopt_mpi)
2059 call dgemm_my('N', 'T', nelorbh, nelorbh, nelorb_c, 1.d0, psip, nelorbh &
2060 &, mu_c, nelorbh, 0.d0, detmat, 2*nelorbh, nprocu, rankopt, commopt_mpi)
2061! down-down
2062 ! Contract down-down block: detmat(nelorbh+1:2*nelorbh, nelorbh+1:2*nelorbh) = mu_c * detmat_c(nelorb_c+1:2*nelorb_c, nelorb_c+1:2*nelorb_c) * mu_c^T
2063 call dgemm_my('N', 'N', nelorbh, nelorb_c, nelorb_c, 1.d0, mu_c, nelorbh &
2064 &, detmat_c(nelorb_c + 1, nelorb_c + 1), 2*nelorb_c, 0.d0, psip, nelorbh, nprocu, rankopt, commopt_mpi)
2065 call dgemm_my('N', 'T', nelorbh, nelorbh, nelorb_c, 1.d0, psip, nelorbh &
2066 &, mu_c, nelorbh, 0.d0, detmat(nelorbh + 1, nelorbh + 1), 2*nelorbh, nprocu, rankopt, commopt_mpi)
2067
2068! down-up
2069 ! Contract down-up block: detmat(nelorbh+1:2*nelorbh, 1:nelorbh) = mu_c * detmat_c(nelorb_c+1:2*nelorb_c, 1:nelorb_c) * mu_c^T
2070 call dgemm_my('N', 'N', nelorbh, nelorb_c, nelorb_c, 1.d0, mu_c, nelorbh &
2071 &, detmat_c(nelorb_c + 1, 1), 2*nelorb_c, 0.d0, psip, nelorbh, nprocu, rankopt, commopt_mpi)
2072 call dgemm_my('N', 'T', nelorbh, nelorbh, nelorb_c, 1.d0, psip, nelorbh &
2073 &, mu_c, nelorbh, 0.d0, detmat(nelorbh + 1, 1), 2*nelorbh, nprocu, rankopt, commopt_mpi)
2074! up-down
2075 ! Contract up-down block: detmat(1:nelorbh, nelorbh+1:2*nelorbh) = mu_c * detmat_c(1:nelorb_c, nelorb_c+1:2*nelorb_c) * mu_c^T
2076 call dgemm_my('N', 'N', nelorbh, nelorb_c, nelorb_c, 1.d0, mu_c, nelorbh &
2077 &, detmat_c(1, nelorb_c + 1), 2*nelorb_c, 0.d0, psip, nelorbh, nprocu, rankopt, commopt_mpi)
2078 call dgemm_my('N', 'T', nelorbh, nelorbh, nelorb_c, 1.d0, psip, nelorbh &
2079 &, mu_c, nelorbh, 0.d0, detmat(1, nelorbh + 1), 2*nelorbh, nprocu, rankopt, commopt_mpi)
2080 end subroutine scontract_genj
2081
2082 ! Contracts Jastrow matrices
2083 ! Parameters:
2084 ! - nelorbh: Number of orbitals per spin channel
2085 ! - nelorb: Total number of orbitals
2086 ! - nelcol: Number of columns
2087 ! - nelorb_c: Number of contracted orbitals
2088 ! - nelcol_c: Number of contracted columns
2089 ! - detmat: Output determinant matrix (nelorb x nelcol)
2090 ! - detmat_c: Input contracted determinant matrix (nelorb_c x nelcol_c)
2091 ! - mu_c: Contraction coefficients (nelorbh x nelorb_c)
2092 ! - psip: Temporary workspace (nelorbh x nelcol_c)
2093 subroutine scontract_mat_jas(nelorbh, nelorb, nelcol, nelorb_c &
2094 &, nelcol_c, detmat, detmat_c, mu_c, psip)
2095 implicit none
2096 integer nelorbh, nelorb, nelorb_c, nelcol, nelcol_c, i
2097 real*8 detmat(nelorb, nelcol), detmat_c(nelorb_c, *) &
2098 &, mu_c(nelorbh, *), psip(nelorbh, *)
2099! WARNING IT REFERS ONLY TO jASTROW SO IPF AND UNPAIRED ARE NOT USEd
2100!#ifdef __CASO
2101! nprocu=nprocopt
2102!#else
2103! nprocu=1
2104!#endif
2105 detmat = 0.d0
2106 ! Perform matrix contractions for Jastrow part: detmat = mu_c * detmat_c * mu_c^T
2107 call dgemm_my('N', 'N', nelorbh, nelcol_c, nelorb_c, 1.d0, mu_c, nelorbh &
2108 &, detmat_c, nelorb_c, 0.d0, psip, nelorbh, nprocu, rankopt, commopt_mpi)
2109 call dgemm_my('N', 'T', nelorbh, nelorbh, nelorb_c, 1.d0, psip, nelorbh &
2110 &, mu_c, nelorbh, 0.d0, detmat, nelorb, nprocu, rankopt, commopt_mpi)
2111 end subroutine scontract_mat_jas
2112
2113 ! Contracts determinant matrices
2114 ! Parameters:
2115 ! - nelorbh: Number of orbitals per spin channel
2116 ! - nelorb: Total number of orbitals
2117 ! - nelcol: Number of columns
2118 ! - nelorb_c: Number of contracted orbitals
2119 ! - nelcol_c: Number of contracted columns
2120 ! - detmat: Output determinant matrix (ipc*ipf*nelorb x nelcol)
2121 ! - detmat_c: Input contracted determinant matrix (ipc*nelorb_c x nelcol_c)
2122 ! - mu_c: Contraction coefficients (ipc*ipf*nelorbh x nelorb_c)
2123 ! - psip: Temporary workspace (ipf*ipc*nelorbh x nelcol_c)
2124 subroutine scontract_mat_det(nelorbh, nelorb, nelcol, nelorb_c &
2125 &, nelcol_c, detmat, detmat_c, mu_c, psip)
2126 implicit none
2127 integer nelorbh, nelorb, nelorb_c, nelcol, nelcol_c, i
2128 real*8 detmat(ipc*ipf*nelorb, nelcol), detmat_c(ipc*nelorb_c, *) &
2129 &, mu_c(ipc*ipf*nelorbh, *), psip(ipf*ipc*nelorbh, *)
2130!#ifdef __CASO
2131! nprocu=nprocopt
2132!#else
2133! nprocu=1
2134!#endif
2135 if (ipc .eq. 2) then
2136 ! Complex case: Use complex BLAS operations (zgemm_my)
2137 detmat = 0.d0
2138 call zgemm_my('N', 'N', ipf*nelorbh, nelcol_c, nelorb_c, (1.d0, 0.d0), mu_c, ipf*nelorbh &
2139 &, detmat_c, nelorb_c, (0.d0, 0.d0), psip, ipf*nelorbh, nprocu, rankopt, commopt_mpi)
2140 call zgemm_my('N', 'T', ipf*nelorbh, ipf*nelorbh, nelorb_c, (1.d0, 0.d0), psip, ipf*nelorbh &
2141 &, mu_c, ipf*nelorbh, (0.d0, 0.d0), detmat, ipf*nelorb, nprocu, rankopt, commopt_mpi)
2142 if (nelcol_c .gt. nelorb_c) then
2143 ! Copy remaining columns for complex case
2144 do i = nelorb_c + 1, nelcol_c
2145 call zcopy(ipf*nelorbh, psip(1, i), 1, detmat(1, ipf*nelorb + i - nelorb_c), 1)
2146 end do
2147 end if
2148 else
2149 ! Real case: Use real BLAS operations (dgemm_my)
2150 detmat = 0.d0
2151 call dgemm_my('N', 'N', ipf*nelorbh, nelcol_c, nelorb_c, 1.d0, mu_c, ipf*nelorbh&
2152 &, detmat_c, nelorb_c, 0.d0, psip, ipf*nelorbh, nprocu, rankopt, commopt_mpi)
2153 call dgemm_my('N', 'T', ipf*nelorbh, ipf*nelorbh, nelorb_c, 1.d0, psip, ipf*nelorbh&
2154 &, mu_c, ipf*nelorbh, 0.d0, detmat, ipf*nelorb, nprocu, rankopt, commopt_mpi)
2155 if (nelcol_c .gt. nelorb_c) then
2156 ! Copy remaining columns for real case
2157 do i = nelorb_c + 1, nelcol_c
2158 call dcopy(ipf*nelorbh, psip(1, i), 1, detmat(1, nelorb*ipf + i - nelorb_c), 1)
2159 end do
2160 end if
2161 end if
2162 end subroutine scontract_mat_det
2163
2164 ! Updates the k-point grid for periodic calculations
2165 ! This subroutine:
2166 ! 1. Initializes direct lattice vectors for periodic basis set
2167 ! 2. Builds lattice vector map for basis set computation
2168 ! 3. Optimizes number of vectors in summation
2169 ! 4. Handles both real and complex wave functions
2170 ! 5. Supports both open and periodic boundary conditions
2171 subroutine update_kgrid
2172 implicit none
2173 integer i, j, ii, jj, kk, ll, count1, count2, count1j, count2j, indpar, indparp, kboundi&
2174 &, ind, kboundi_max, iii, jjj, kkk, k, maxdim
2175 integer, dimension(:, :), allocatable :: kshell_map
2176 real*8 kbound, map_tmp(3, 27), max_rejected, cost_tilted
2177 logical, external :: slaterorb
2178 logical not_found
2179 integer, dimension(:, :), allocatable :: kpip_sav
2180
2181 ! Initialize direct lattice vectors for periodic basis set
2182 ! Uses same definition as Crystal DFT code
2183 ! Can be used for both real and complex wave functions
2184 ! For complex wave functions, can also handle open systems
2185 ! Use "PBC_C" keyword in wave function first line to enable
2186 if (allocated(kgrid)) deallocate (kgrid)
2187 if (allocated(kgrid_atom)) deallocate (kgrid_atom)
2188 ikshift = nshell
2189 if (abs(lbox) .eq. 3.d0) then
2190 ! Determine the maximum number of direct lattice vectors for each shell
2191 ! This is based on the basis set parameters and cutoff criteria
2192 if (yes_crystalj) then
2193 allocate (kshell_map(3, nshell + nshellj))
2194 else
2195 allocate (kshell_map(3, nshell))
2196 end if
2197 kshell_map = 0
2198 indpar = 0
2199 do i = 1, nshell
2200 indparp = indpar + 1
2201 if (lepsbas .gt. 0.d0) then
2202 do j = 1, 3
2203 if (cellscale(j) .ne. 0.d0) then

2614 ! =============================================
2615 ! norm_metric - Calculate Norm Using Metric Tensor
2616 ! =============================================
2617 ! Purpose: Calculates the norm of a 3D vector using a given metric tensor
2618 !
2619 ! Mathematical Definition:
2620 ! ||r||_metric = sqrt(r^T * metric * r)
2621 ! where r is a 3D vector and metric is a 3x3 symmetric matrix
2622 !
2623 ! Parameters:
2624 ! - r: 3D position vector (input)
2625 ! - metric: 3x3 metric tensor (input)
2626 ! Returns: Norm of the vector in the given metric (real*8)
2627 !
2628 ! Algorithm:
2629 ! 1. Compute quadratic form: r^T * metric * r
2630 ! 2. Take square root with protection from roundoff errors
2631 ! 3. Return the norm
2632 !
2633 ! Usage:
2634 ! This function is used in periodic boundary condition calculations
2635 ! to determine the distance between lattice points in a general metric
2636 function norm_metric(r, metric)
2637 implicit none
2638 real*8 norm_metric, r(3), metric(3, 3)
2639 ! Calculate norm using metric tensor: ||r|| = sqrt(r^T * metric * r)
2640 norm_metric = metric(1, 1)*r(1)*r(1) + metric(2, 2)*r(2)*r(2) + metric(3, 3)*r(3)*r(3)&
2641 & + 2.d0*(metric(1, 2)*r(1)*r(2) + metric(1, 3)*r(1)*r(3) + metric(2, 3)*r(2)*r(3))
2642 norm_metric = dsqrt(max(norm_metric, 0.d0)) ! Protection from roundoff errors
2643 return
2644 end
2645
2646end module allio

2648! =============================================
2649! prep_map - Prepare Mapping of Lattice Vectors
2650! =============================================
2651! Purpose: Prepares mapping of lattice vectors for periodic boundary condition calculations
2652!
2653! Algorithm:
2654! 1. For each coordinate (x, y, z), there are three possible minimum positions:
2655! - Current position (when coordinate is zero)
2656! - Lower boundary (-L/2)
2657! - Upper boundary (+L/2)
2658! 2. This results in 27 possible combinations (3^3)
2659! 3. The function generates all these combinations to find the minimum distance
2660!
2661! Mathematical Background:
2662! When computing distances in periodic systems, the minimum distance
2663! between two points can occur at different positions within the unit cell.
2664! This subroutine explores all possible combinations to find the true minimum.
2665!
2666! Parameters:
2667! - map_tmp: Array to store mapped vectors (3 x 3 x 3 x 3)
2668! - cellscale: Cell scaling factors (3)
2669!
2670! Output:
2671! - map_tmp: Contains all 27 possible vector positions for distance calculation
2672subroutine prep_map(map_tmp, cellscale)
2673 implicit none
2674 real*8 map_tmp(3, 3, 3, 3), cellscale(3), cellhalf(3, 3)
2675 integer i, j, k
2676 ! Find possible minimum of the metric
2677 ! For each coordinate there are two possibilities:
2678 ! 1. Minimum at boundary +/- L/2
2679 ! 2. Minimum at current position (when zero)
2680 ! Results in 27 possibilities (3 for each coordinate)
2681 ! including the input map(:,1,1,1)
2682 cellhalf(:, 1) = 0.d0
2683 cellhalf(:, 2) = -cellscale(:)/2.d0
2684 cellhalf(:, 3) = cellscale(:)/2.d0
2685
2686 ! Generate all possible combinations of boundary conditions
2687 do i = 1, 3
2688 do j = 1, 3
2689 do k = 1, 3
2690 map_tmp(1, i, j, k) = map_tmp(1, 1, 1, 1) + cellhalf(1, i)
2691 map_tmp(2, i, j, k) = map_tmp(2, 1, 1, 1) + cellhalf(2, j)
2692 map_tmp(3, i, j, k) = map_tmp(3, 1, 1, 1) + cellhalf(3, k)
2693 end do
2694 end do
2695 end do
2696 return
2697end
prep_map
